tasks.short: Post warning signs and lock doors before fumigation.

steps.what: Write fumigation warning signs for this building
Post the signs and lock doors to secure the fumigated area

tasks.design: The pest control worker writes the fumigation warning on the signs, then walks the building, posts a sign at each entrance and locks the doors. The clearance stays with the worker because a person left inside would be harmed. No system is added, and the walk is not shortened.
tasks.previous_blocker: The building has to be empty and every door locked before gas is released, and that check only happens on site.
tasks.enabler_now: Warning signs and door locks are already how this clearance is done. Nothing new removes the walk.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding the area is empty, and finding an entrance that was missed, stays with the worker at the building.
tasks.human_edge: The worker can see whether a person, a pet or an open door is still there. A written sign does not make that check.
tasks.altitude: The pest control worker still writes each warning, walks the entrances, posts the signs and locks the doors. No time is removed and no new decision right is added.

reach.role: Pesticide Handlers, Sprayers, and Applicators, Vegetation
reach.task: Keep people out of a treated area until re-entry is allowed
reach.learn: Which entrances must carry a warning before a fumigant is released

evidence.claim: Posting fumigation warning signs and locking doors is physical work at the building, and a missed entrance can leave a person inside the treated area.
National pesticide rules differ, and this design does not replace the clearance the worker must make before fumigation.

assumptions: Means sum to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 0, spreadsheets 0, mail 0, documents 5 and in-person 95. Screens were 0.1 and mail 0.4, so this task has no mailbox step and no screen step. There is no calculation table.

The document share is writing the warning on the signs: fumigant, date, start and the time the building may be re-entered. That writing stays at full time because no system already holds those fields. Standard software for this task is none.
The in-person share is the walk: confirm the area is empty, post a sign at each entrance and lock the doors. That step stays at full time. No mechanism posts the signs or turns the locks.
The signs address occupants and passers-by, not the fumigation crew. Posting them is the outward act. There is no separate message and no record commit, so there is no extra gate.
Focal upkeep is zero. No system is added and the worker does not gain a new weekly chore. The door-by-door check is already inside the walk.
unknowns: Whether this employer fumigates whole buildings or single rooms, and how many entrances a typical job has.
Whether occupants are told only by the posted signs.
research_questions: How often a second walk finds a door without a sign or still unlocked?
What particulars does this employer require on the warning before gas is released?

already_counted.description: Walking each entrance to confirm a warning sign is posted and the door is locked before fumigation.

incremental.description: No new weekly chore. No system is added for this clearance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shorter. The worker still writes each warning, posts the signs and locks the doors, because the clearance is whether the building is empty.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
